title: ENISA NIS360 - Cybersecurity Maturity and Criticality of High-Criticality Sectors
summary: This report assesses the cybersecurity maturity and criticality of high-criticality sectors under the NIS2 directive. Maturity is measured by the effectiveness and consistency in managing cybersecurity risks, while criticality considers factors like economic importance and severe consequences from attacks.
description: ENISA uses a structured methodology to evaluate the maturity and criticality of nine sectors: Energy, Digital Infrastructure, Transport, Finance, Health, ICT Service Management, Public Administrations, Space, and Drinking/Waste Water. The report highlights improvements in cybersecurity across sectors but notes uneven progress.
causes: Improvements due to evolving policy requirements, increased political attention, and advancements in cybersecurity legislation. Factors such as skill shortages, sector-specific characteristics, and organizational size contribute to variations in maturity.
actions: ENISA's structured methodology for assessing maturity and criticality includes evaluating legislative effectiveness, company preparedness, authority institutional capacity, and the effectiveness of sectoral ecosystem structures. Regular updates ensure current state assessments.
lessons_learned: Despite improvements, maturity remains uneven across sectors. Skill shortages and sector-specific challenges contribute to these differences. Improved information sharing, stronger collaboration, and better risk management are key drivers for positive development in some sectors.
recommendations: More sectors may move out of the 'risk zone' as cybersecurity legislation, perceived cyber risk, threat exposure, interdependencies, and ecosystem expectations continue to drive investment and preparedness efforts.
